pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

This PR contains several changes to allow users to fetch newly created dashboards and folders. 

The changes are:
* on client side: remove the use of authLib cache when running authZ service in-proc
* on server side: add a denial cache to return quickly when we know that a user does not have permission on a specific resource
* on server side: if permission denial cache is not hit, and the requested resource is not found in cached permissions, requery permissions from the DB

**Why do we need this feature?**

Otherwise dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana users

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/identity-access-team/issues/1316
pr.title: AuthZService: improve authz caching

raw_findings.body: The renderer request is denied from the negative cache even though renderer identities are granted wildcard dashboard/folder read permissions.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The early negative-cache return bypasses renderer permission resolution and returns `Allowed: false` for an otherwise authorized request.
raw_findings.impact: The renderer request is denied from the negative cache even though renderer identities are granted wildcard dashboard/folder read permissions.
raw_findings.root_cause: The negative-cache key includes the parsed user identifier but omits identity type; both anonymous and renderer identities use identifier `0`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include `checkReq.IdentityType` in the denial-cache key (and update `userPermDenialCacheKey` and its callers) so entries cannot be shared across identity types.
raw_findings.title: Denial cache conflates anonymous and renderer identities
raw_findings.trigger: An `anonymous:0` check for a dashboard or folder is denied and cached, then a `render:0` check requests the same namespace, read action, name, and parent folder before the 30-second denial TTL expires.

raw_findings.body: The test still observes a denial because the cached scope is false, so CI will not detect a regression where an explicit denial-cache entry fails to override an otherwise allowed permission.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The test's expected denial is produced by normal permission evaluation even without the feature it claims to cover.
raw_findings.impact: The test still observes a denial because the cached scope is false, so CI will not detect a regression where an explicit denial-cache entry fails to override an otherwise allowed permission.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fixture intended to prove that permission evaluation is bypassed configures the target scope as denied rather than allowed.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set `"dashboards:uid:dash1"` to `true` (and retain the matching folder setup if needed) so the assertion only passes when the denial cache short-circuits the normal allow path.
raw_findings.title: Negative-cache test does not establish that the cached permission would allow access
raw_findings.trigger: The denial-cache lookup is removed or stops matching entries while this test continues to run.

finding.title: Denial cache conflates anonymous and renderer identities
finding.trigger: An `anonymous:0` check for a dashboard or folder is denied and cached, then a `render:0` check requests the same namespace, read action, name, and parent folder before the 30-second denial TTL expires.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that anonymous and renderer identities share identifier '0' causing cache key collision is speculative. The cache key includes userUID which comes from checkReq.UserUID, but the code shows different identity types (TypeAnonymous vs TypeRenderService) are handled separately in getCachedIdentityPermissions (lines 346-367) and getIdentityPermissions (lines 330-339). For renderer, getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound immediately (line 354), so renderer checks never use the permDenialCache lookup result - they fall through to getRendererPermissions which returns wildcard permissions. The denial cache entry from anonymous would not affect renderer because renderer bypasses the cached permission path entirely.

finding.title: Negative-cache test does not establish that the cached permission would allow access
finding.trigger: The denial-cache lookup is removed or stops matching entries while this test continues to run.
finding.verifier_reason: The test comment at line 981 says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' but the value set is `false` not `true`. However, this does not make the test ineffective as claimed. The test correctly verifies that permDenialCache short-circuits before permCache is consulted - the permCache value being false or true is irrelevant because the denial cache lookup at line 117 returns early with Allowed:false before getCachedIdentityPermissions is called. The test would still fail if the denial cache lookup were removed because then permCache would be checked and return false anyway, but the test's purpose (verify denial cache takes precedence) is still valid since removal would change the code path taken.
